metaDescription: Two true DeWalt 20V handheld vacuums and two compact wet/dry units compared on filtration, tank size, bare-tool pricing and who each one really suits.
expertTake: The DeWalt 20V HEPA handheld is the best pick for anyone who sands drywall or cuts masonry, because its filter is built for fine dust. The wet/dry hand vac is the pick if spills are part of the job. Anyone who wants a full cordless shop vacuum should look at the two-gallon units below, and anyone who wants a household crumb catcher should buy something else.
introParagraphs: This maker does not offer many handheld vacuums, and that scarcity is a clue to who they are for. They are tool-platform machines that run on the same 20V packs as the drills and saws on the truck, built to clear dust off benches, tools and cab seats between jobs rather than to tidy a living room.

The range is small enough to be confusing. Some listings are dry only, some are wet or dry, some arrive as bare tools without a battery, and two are portable vacuums that sit one size above a true handheld. Knowing the difference before buying matters more than any suction rating, and it also decides whether the purchase is a bargain or an incomplete kit.

products.name: DeWalt 20V handheld vacuum with HEPA filter and 6 attachments
products.description:
This is the machine that justifies buying a DeWalt handheld at all. Its HEPA filter is aimed at fine job dust such as concrete and drywall, particle sizes that a basic foam filter lets straight through into the room. If you work indoors around finished surfaces, a filter that holds that dust is the difference between a clean site and a hazy one.

It runs on the DeWalt 20V battery family, so a pack from your drill drives it, and the listing quotes a long run with a large pack. Six attachments and an LED light cover benches, truck interiors and corners that a bare nozzle cannot reach. A push-button canister release empties it quickly between tasks, which matters when you do it many times a day. It is dry only, so the wet/dry hand vac below handles the liquids this one must never touch.

Fine dust loads a HEPA element fast, so plan on tapping it out outdoors and rinsing or replacing it more often than you would a household filter. Wipe the filter seat so the element seals properly each time you refit it. For a solo tradesperson, it is the most useful small tool in the lineup, and the one most likely to be borrowed by the rest of the crew. A useful habit is to keep a spare element in the toolbox, since changing a clogged filter takes seconds and restores full airflow on the spot.
products.bestFor: Tradespeople who sand, cut or drill and need to catch fine dust.
pros: HEPA filter for fine construction dust
Six attachments and an LED light
cons: Fine dust clogs the HEPA element quickly

products.name: DeWalt 20V MAX wet or dry hand vacuum, 1/2-gallon tank
products.description:
Where the HEPA unit above is a dust specialist, this one is a generalist. It is rated for wet and dry cleanup, which means a spilled drink, a puddle under a sink or a leak of coolant is no longer a reason to put the vacuum away. The listing describes a washable HEPA-class wet/dry filter that traps fine particles at a rated efficiency.

Two cleanup modes cover most jobs: a front utility nozzle for floors and benches, and an extendable rubber hose for engine bays, vents and tight cabinets. The half-gallon tank is larger than any household dustbuster bowl, but it is a fraction of the two-gallon units later in this guide, so it sits in the middle of the range for capacity. A heavy-duty latch holds the tank on during a knock, which is a real plus on a site.

It is sold bare tool, so battery and charger cost extra unless a kit is listed, and it is a poor value for someone who has no DeWalt packs yet. After wet use, empty the tank, rinse it and leave the lid off so the filter dries fully, because a damp filter in a closed tank grows mould within days. For a plumber or a mechanic it is the most versatile tool here, and for a carpenter who only makes dry dust, it is more than they need. The extendable hose is the hidden strength: it lets you pull dust out of a vent or a gap behind a cabinet where the front nozzle cannot go, and it is far easier to aim than a rigid crevice tool. In a service van it also doubles as a spill kit, because one tool covers dust at the start of a job and a leaked drip at the end.
products.bestFor: Plumbers, mechanics and installers who meet both liquid spills and dust.
pros: Rated for wet or dry cleanup
cons: Bare tool, battery and charger extra
Damp filter must be dried fully

products.name: DeWalt 20V MAX cordless 2-gallon wet/dry shop vacuum

specList.label: Class
specList.value: Portable shop vac, not a handheld

products.description:
This is not a handheld, and a guide on handhelds should say so plainly. It is a small cordless shop vacuum, carried by a handle, with a two-gallon tank four times the size of the hand vac's half-gallon. It is here because buyers searching for a DeWalt hand vacuum often really want something with more capacity than a dustbuster.

The listing describes a HEPA-rated wet/dry filter at 99.97 percent efficiency at 0.3 microns, a tank that holds enough for a large clean-up and a washable filter that is quick to service. It trades the one-hand portability of the true handhelds for volume, so you stop less often to empty. The extra weight shows when the tank is full of wet debris.

Empty it before it is full, since a two-gallon tank of liquid is heavy to carry. Rinse the tank and let the filter dry with the lid off. It makes more sense than a handheld for garage floors, van interiors and small workshops, and less sense for desks and shelves. Because it uses the same pack as the smaller hand vacs, a single large battery can serve both, though it will drain faster under the bigger motor load. If you often clean up after plumbing or flood work, the larger tank is a practical gain, since you can finish a job without a trip to the drain.
products.bestFor: Garages and vans where a handheld's tank is too small.

products.name: DeWalt 20V MAX 2-gallon shop vacuum, cordless or corded

specList.label: Class
specList.value: Portable shop vac, not a handheld

products.description:
This second two-gallon unit adds one clever feature: it runs from a 20V MAX battery or from a wall cord. That removes the main fear about cordless shop vacuums, which is a dead pack in the middle of a long clean-up. Plug in at the garage and keep going, or unplug for the van and roof.

Like the other two-gallon DeWalt, it is a portable shop vacuum, not a handheld, and the listing describes a wide nozzle and enough capacity to empty a toilet or a clogged pipe. A reusable washable filter and on-board accessory storage keep the kit together. Compared with the cordless-only model, the dual power makes it the more flexible choice for a mixed workload.

When using the cord, unroll it fully to avoid heat build-up, and keep the battery off the charger while working so it does not overheat. Empty the tank before it fills and dry the filter after wet jobs. It is a good fit for a hobby workshop, less so for someone who needs only a quick bench clean. The cord option also lets the battery stay on a charger on the shelf, so a spare pack is ready when you carry the vacuum to a job without a power point. Compared with the cordless-only unit above, it is the safer choice for a shop where long sanding sessions are routine and a flat battery would stop the work.
products.bestFor: Shops and garages that want one vacuum for cord or battery operation.
pros: Runs corded or on a 20V MAX battery
cons: Cord limits reach when plugged in

buyingCriteria.explanation: The HEPA handheld and the 1/2-gallon wet/dry hand vac are true one-hand units. The two 2-gallon models are carried by a handle and hold four times the debris. Decide by the biggest job you do, because a hand vac that fills in a minute is more annoying than a heavier one that does not.

The HEPA handheld is dry only, while the hand vac and both 2-gallon units handle liquid. A dry-only machine can be ruined by a spill, so a trade that meets water should pay for a wet rating. A wet-capable filter also needs more careful drying. Tradespeople who rarely meet liquid can save the extra care by choosing the dry HEPA handheld, while anyone who works near water should pay for the rating and treat it as a safety margin against an unplanned spill.

Concrete and drywall dust include fine particles that foam filters do not stop. The listings describe HEPA or HEPA-class elements at about 99.97 percent at 0.3 microns. A filter helps only if the seat seals properly, so clean the gasket regularly. Concrete dust in particular is abrasive and silica-bearing, so treat any vacuum used on it as part of a wider dust control plan that also includes damp cutting, a mask where required and a clean-up routine that does not blow dust back into the air.

These are DeWalt 20V tools, and several are sold as bare tools without a pack or charger. If you already own 20V batteries, the vacuum is a bargain, and if not, the missing parts erase the saving. Always read the listing for battery and charger. A 5Ah-class pack runs these vacuums much longer than a compact 2Ah pack, and the listing for the HEPA handheld quotes its long run with a large battery. Budget for the pack that matches your workload, not the one that was cheapest in the kit.

A 1/2-gallon tank is light and quick, while a 2-gallon tank holds more but is heavy when wet. Empty at half full on liquids. Match the tank to the mess, not to the biggest number. The 1/2-gallon tank of the hand vac suits a bench, while the 2-gallon tank on the shop-style units suits a floor, and a half-full wet tank in either is heavier than it looks. Carry weight is the cost of capacity, so choose the smallest tank that lets you finish a typical job without a trip to the drain.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Not all DeWalt-compatible vacuums are DeWalt
buyingCriteria.explanation: Many adapter vacuums are advertised as working with DeWalt batteries, but they are third-party products with their own warranty. Those listings appear alongside the genuine ones and are not covered in this guide. Buy a genuine unit if you want brand support.

specDecoder.watchFor: The 2-gallon units are portable vacs, not handhelds.

specDecoder.meaning: A wet-rated unit has a filter and motor protection suited to liquid.
specDecoder.watchFor: The HEPA handheld is dry only.

specDecoder.meaning: A bare tool is the machine alone, with no battery or charger.
specDecoder.watchFor: The hand vac is sold as a bare tool.

specDecoder.meaning: A dual-power unit can run from a battery or a wall outlet, which solves run time on long jobs.

howWeEvaluated.title: Filtration
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated filter type against fine job dust, based on the spec sheet language in each listing. The HEPA handheld and the HEPA-class wet/dry units ranked highest. Standard foam filters were not part of this lineup, so the ranking turned on filter size, washability and how easy the element is to refit without a gap.

howWeEvaluated.title: Wet and dry capability
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked which models are rated for liquid. Three of four handle wet pickup, which matters in plumbing and automotive work. The dry-only handheld was graded for dust.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and carry
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared a 1/2-gallon tank with two 2-gallon tanks. Smaller tanks won on portability, larger ones on stopping less often. Task size decided the ranking.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power options
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at battery-only versus corded or cordless operation. The dual-power unit earned credit for flexibility. Bare-tool listings lost points for new buyers.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We read owner feedback patterns on filter clogging, latch durability and battery cost. DeWalt tools draw praise for durability. Price tier ordered the list only.

cards.label: Handheld
cards.text: The HEPA unit and the half-gallon wet/dry hand vac are quick one-hand tools. They fill fast and are best for benches, cabs and small spills.

cards.label: 2-gallon portable
cards.text: The two shop-style units hold four times as much and handle floors. They are heavier and carried by handle.

howToChoose.note: Pick a handheld for tools and benches, and a 2-gallon unit for floors and large spills.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for a HEPA element, a sealing filter seat and a canister that empties without a dust cloud.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The DeWalt 20V HEPA handheld is the pick, with the wet/dry hand vac as the alternative if you also meet liquid.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more on the HEPA handheld if you work indoors every day. Fine dust is the reason it exists.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save with the wet/dry hand vac if you already own DeWalt packs and need only occasional cleanup.

maintenance.why: A full tank loses airflow and adds weight. Wet debris should be emptied the same day.
Fine dust clogs HEPA media fast. A clogged filter is the main cause of weak suction.
A damp filter in a closed tank grows mould. Leave the lid off to dry.
Hoses split at the flex and latches pick up grit. Replace early to keep the seal.
Lithium packs fade when hot or empty. Keep them off truck dashboards.

faq.a: The 20V HEPA handheld is best for fine dust, and the wet/dry hand vac is best for liquids. Choose by the mess you make most often.

faq.q: Do the listings include a battery?
faq.a: Many are bare tools. Look for the words kit, battery or charger on the listing, and plan to buy a 20V pack if you do not own one. A larger pack runs a vacuum noticeably longer than a compact one, so size the battery to the job.
No. They are portable shop vacuums carried by a handle. They are included because many buyers searching for a DeWalt hand vac actually want more capacity.

faq.q: What about vacuums made for DeWalt batteries?
faq.a: Those are third-party products sold as compatible with DeWalt packs. They are not DeWalt machines and are not ranked here.

faq.q: Can the HEPA handheld pick up water?
faq.a: No, it is dry only. Use the wet/dry hand vac or a 2-gallon model for liquids.

faq.q: How long do the batteries last?
faq.a: Expect several years of regular use before capacity fades. Heat and deep discharge shorten that, so store packs indoors and avoid leaving them on a hot dashboard. A pack that fades is cheap to swap compared with replacing a sealed household vacuum.
